RT Quinn Thompson I don't see many offering alternatives to the Trump policy agenda with regards to fixing the income inequality but I still see many not understanding the why. This table might help explain. Since 2023, foreign born employment has grown >2x more than native born, despite the native born employment level being >4x the size. Given the strong correlation between this data and border crossings, it is very clear in showing that illegal immigration and an open border policy has hurt lower and middle income American workers' competitive position in the labor market as well as hampered their wage growth. While this is both pro-growth and disinflationary, the benefits accrue to corporations via higher profits and the wealthy upper class via higher stock prices at the expense of the lower and middle class who suffer wage stagnation and low job growth. If this strikes a chord with you, I would like to understand why as I have tried to write this as objectively and factual as possible. I don't know what the right answer is but I understand why there's a major class divide in the country and interest in change from large parts of the US population. The Trump policy agenda is simply implementing what they believe they have been elected to do.
